identity.real_world_identity_notes: Formula Vee, the low-cost open-wheel category built from Volkswagen Beetle parts. Cars use the Beetle 1600 engine of about 70 to 75 hp and the VW four-speed gearbox, sealed and restricted to reliability modifications.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift and blips to downshift.

The gearbox is the Volkswagen Beetle four-speed transaxle, which the registered source describes as constant-mesh with balk ring synchronisers on all four forward gears. A downshift blip is therefore authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear, so it is recorded as optional.
The gate is recorded unknown. The driver could not read it in the cockpit, and no reviewed source describes the shift pattern of a Formula Vee, so neither the drive nor the sources establish it.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.formula-vee-gen1.20260815t231602548z-d616fb3b by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the category's Volkswagen basis, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The category source gives a VW four-speed gearbox and the transaxle source describes that unit as constant-mesh with balk ring synchronisers, and the live drive selected four H-pattern gears with no automatic cut or blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Formula Vee runs the Beetle's VW four-speed, a constant-mesh transaxle with balk-ring synchronisers on all four forward gears, so the blip eases the synchros but the gear engages without it.
